note: G2 frozen routing corpus. Every probe names the candidate skills it routes among (a bounded corpus), the expected routed id sequence, and the leader's score as measured from the real scorer at freeze time. Descriptions are hashed: an edit that changes a candidate's text fails the drift check first, and the probe that depended on it fails next. Expectations are only ever updated deliberately, in the same change that edits the description.

rules.ordering: score descending, then distinctive name-token count descending, then name ascending
rules.floor: a skill scoring below minScore (0.2 by default) is not routed
rules.tie: an exact score tie is broken by specificity and then by name, never by candidate order or insertion order
rules.noMatch: an empty result is a valid outcome; the resolver never falls back to a default skill
rules.invalid: a file whose frontmatter has no `name` is refused by the parser and never registered
rules.fanout: a `*-automation` wrapper with no distinctive service token in the prompt is clamped below the floor, so a generic mention cannot fan out across hundreds of integrations

invalidSkill.reason: the frontmatter has no `name`, so parseSkillMarkdown returns null and the file must never reach the registry

probes.note: the hyphenated name appears verbatim: 0.6 for the name, 0.22 for two distinctive tokens, 0.12 for matching all of them
the same skill is reached without the hyphens, which is what a user actually types
